product.name: Canon
product.lede: Canon is a formal language and a deterministic calculus for evidence-governed protocols. For one case under one protocol it answers what is known, what is unknown, which obligations remain open, which actions are admissible, and whether an outcome has been earned.
product.meta: Rust · protocol/1 source · canon-ir/1 compiled form · Apache-2.0
product.terminalCaption: Real canon output, recorded by canon-docs and checked for drift on every change.

sections.title: Legitimacy, not sequencing.
sections.lede: A workflow answers what executes next. Canon answers what is currently legitimate: the claims that can be made, the evidence that can establish them, the actions that are possible and the outcomes a case may conclude under. It does not execute anything.

items.title: Declared as data
items.description: A protocol is a YAML document in the protocol/1 format. Canon parses it, checks every reference and compiles it into canon-ir/1, a normalized form stable enough to hash.

items.title: Pure and deterministic
items.description: The library reads no clock, environment, network or filesystem. Callers pass documents in; the same normalized input gives the same normalized output.

items.title: Three-valued claims
items.description: Every claim is TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN. Missing evidence leaves a claim UNKNOWN; it never makes it FALSE.

sections.title: From a document to a decision.
sections.lede: Each step is a command that runs today. The evaluation reads a case snapshot and an evidence set and prints a canon-decision/1 document with a value for every claim.

sections.title: What a protocol declares, as a graph.
sections.lede: The investigation protocol from Canon's own fixtures, drawn from its compiled form. Actions may produce evidence; evidence establishes claims; claims earn outcomes. Hover a node to trace what it rests on.

sections.title: Bootstrap. Here is exactly what exists.
sections.lede: Shipped means a command or library call that runs today. Decided means recorded in an accepted architecture decision, not built. Planned means on the roadmap only.

items.label: protocol/1 source model and parser
items.detail: Unknown keys and explicit nulls are refused.

items.label: Deterministic validation
items.detail: References, duplicates and claim cycles, in a stable order.

items.label: Three-valued claim evaluation
items.detail: canon evaluate over a case snapshot and an evidence directory.

items.label: canon conform run
items.detail: Runs canon-conformance/1 scenarios; nine ship today: CANON-CLAIM-001 (also covering -002), CANON-EVIDENCE-001, -002 and -003, CANON-OBLIGATION-001, CANON-AUTHORITY-001, CANON-OUTCOME-001 and -002, and CANON-EXPLAIN-001 (also covering CANON-DETERMINISM-001).

items.label: Cases compose at run time
items.detail: Child cases and their outcomes as evidence; Atlas ADR 0081.

items.label: Evidence bound to revisions
items.detail: Evidence applies only to the current revision of the artifact it names; scenario CANON-EVIDENCE-001.

items.label: Subject-bound evidence matches
items.detail: An evidence match may name the artifact its record must be about; a record about another artifact does not match it; scenario CANON-EVIDENCE-003.

items.label: Evidence freshness
items.detail: Evidence older than its kind's max_age at the --at instant is excluded, never FALSE; scenario CANON-EVIDENCE-002.

items.label: Obligations
items.detail: Each obligation is open or discharged by its discharge predicate; scenario CANON-OBLIGATION-001.

items.label: Action admissibility
items.detail: Admissible, approval-required or blocked, from preconditions and authority decisions; scenario CANON-AUTHORITY-001.

items.label: Outcomes
items.detail: Legitimate or blocked; no completion through an undeclared or blocked outcome; scenario CANON-OUTCOME-001.

items.label: Decision-based outcomes
items.detail: An outcome may require an explicit decision taken at the current case revision; scenario CANON-OUTCOME-002.

items.label: Structured explanation
items.detail: Every decision says what it was computed from and why each value is what it is, down to the evidence records that applied or were excluded; scenario CANON-EXPLAIN-001.

items.label: canon check
items.detail: Every state of a protocol's finite state space: unreachable outcomes, unsatisfiable preconditions, unproduced evidence, authority bypasses with a witness state, and failing properties with a counterexample.

items.label: Semantic diff
items.detail: Classify a protocol change as tightening, relaxation or breaking.
